checks: Recomputed all quoted ratios from the integrals in out/q52/s320.txt (e.g. 1-0 2.5" N HCN/HCO+ 135.1/148.1=0.912, S 61.2/104.7=0.585; CN=G1+G2 N 235.6/135.1=1.74, S 79.0/61.2=1.29; 3-2 1.4" S HNC/HCN 17.6/26.5=0.66; N/S of line integrals and of line/continuum in s322). Arithmetic agrees with the summary and with the report entries.

Robustness: results are stable to the beam (2.5" vs 3.5"), to the window (350 vs 250 km/s, <=3%), and to the independent project (00412 vs 00993: HNC/HCN N/S 1.23 vs 1.22), with a common-beam convention, line-free baselines and per-pixel fixed N/S positions. Statistical errors are tiny, so the conclusions rest on systematics, which the worker lists honestly (cross-project flux scale and uv coverage cancel in N/S only to first order).

The conclusion that the contrast is not HCN-specific is supported: HCN, HNC and CN all fall by 1.5-3x at S relative to HCO+, and HCO+/continuum is equal at N and S while the N-bearing group is 2-3x lower relative to the continuum at S. I agree. I also agree that no XDR signature is seen (CN/HCN is lower at S, and HCN does not fall alone), and that CN/HCN N/S>1 is in the sense of Harada's Table 13 and Ledger's N value ~1.7.

The ordering of the drop at S (CN > HNC > HCN > HCO+) does not follow critical density (CN has the lowest n_crit of the three), so excitation alone is disfavoured. This is stated and is a useful constraint. The 1-0 vs 3-2 inconsistency of HNC/HCN (N/S 1.22 vs 0.86) is flagged by the worker as a possible uv/recovery issue; at matched 2.5" it is 1.17+-0.10, i.e. consistent with 1-0, so the 1.4" value should not be quoted as a physical difference.
notes_for_questioner: (1) The result points to a composition difference concentrated in the N-bearing/PDR-like group (CN, HCN, HNC) rather than in HCN alone. Test it with an independent column reference: C18O/13CO (matched beam, other ALMA projects on NGC 3256) or H13CO+/H13CN where detectable, so the 'deficit at S' is not tied to the 1.1 mm continuum, which may contain free-free or AGN emission at S. (2) CN is far more sensitive to UV/PDR and to hyperfine opacity than HCN: a two-component RADEX with CN hyperfine ratios (G2/G1 = 1.64 at N, 1.72 at S in 1-0, versus the thin value ~2) would give the CN opacity and temperature at each nucleus and show whether CN/HCN is a column or an excitation effect. (3) HNC/HCN lower at S in 1-0 (warmer gas) against the colder S preferred by the RADEX of p0056 remains unresolved. A matched-beam fit to HCN, HCO+, HNC and CN ladders together, with the HNC 3-2 uv-matched, would settle this. (4) Could the S HCO+ include outflow or shock-enhanced emission (the S outflow is bright in HCO+; Michiyama+2018)? A velocity-resolved N/S ratio (core vs wings) would check whether the HCO+ is boosted in S rather than N-species depleted; the continuum comparison disfavours this, but the wing test is cheap.
